risks.title: Cyberattacks by state-sponsored actors
risks.score_rationale: The risk is cited first and described as originating from sophisticated adversaries, notably nation-states. The language is strong (critical infrastructure targeted). Xcel Energy is a critical infrastructure asset, which increases severity. Highly weighted category in the utilities sector.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party suppliers
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions risks related to security incidents at suppliers. While assessments are performed, exposure persists. The risk is mentioned multiple times, indicating its importance. Less severe than a direct attack.

risks.title: NERC standards compliance
risks.score_rationale: Compliance with NERC standards (critical infrastructure protection) is mandatory and recurring. Non-compliance could result in sanctions. The text underscores alignment with NIST, showing constant vigilance.

risks.title: IT infrastructure failure
risks.score_rationale: Operations depend on IT infrastructure and sophisticated control systems. A failure could interrupt service. The risk is implicit but fundamental, mentioned at the outset of the risk factor.

risks.title: Physical risks to critical assets
risks.score_rationale: The text includes physical security of assets (generation, storage, transmission) in risk assessment. While less detailed than cyber, this is a clear component of the NERC framework.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence was found in the text.
